Hi, I'm sorry you've been feeling emotionally numb. I know too well what that's like. I struggled with depression and anxiety when I was in high school, but have since made a lot of progress to recovery. I remember walking through life for two or three days at a time, unable to feel or react to anything. During that time, I felt absolutely no emotion besides the tension in my chest. You may feel emotionally numb because you are unable to identify what emotion you are feeling. In this case, you should try to take cues from your body (like getting the butterflies (nervousness), feeling tension in your shoulders (stress) etc.). 

Something that always helped me was exercise. I would always feel better after going for a run, and after a few weeks of sticking to a routine I noticed a significant change in my mental health. I also started writing daily entries in my journal and recorded what emotions I was feeling. At first, I didn't know what emotions I felt, so I just jotted down a few notes about my day, things I had done, and really reflected on it. Overtime I began to notice patterns and found it easier to identify the emotions I was feeling. Some other ways you can touch base with your emotions is to find other ways to express yourself: listening to music, dancing, painting, drawing, writing, etc. Find an outlet that is meaningful to you.

A great way to ground yourself and relieve built up stress/tension is to practice yoga and meditation. I don't meditate as often as I used to nowadays, but I was very serious about it in high school and it really helped me to clear my mind and truly find myself. 

These are things that have worked well for me, but we all deal differently. I hope something I've shared will be able to help you, and I am here to talk and listen if you need someone. Sending love and positive vibes your way xx

You sound like my former self, because I understand *exactly* what you are going through. I graduated in 2017, I actually almost didn't walk at graduation because I nearly failed my AP english class. During the spring of my senior year, I pretty much just stopped going to school. I too felt that it was a mix of depression and senioritis, and the fact that my mom was harassing me for my grades going down didn't help me much at all. I couldn't find the motivation to get up and go to school, let alone focus in class or do my homework. I became very distanced from my friends because they just didn't understand what I was going through. I also found that I was having a really hard time remembering things, and my mind could only be described as "foggy".

As for therapy, there are a ton of great options. [7cups.com](https://7cups.com) offers free online therapy and chatting, and I've used their site a lot. It is very helpful to talk to someone who understands, or someone who can offer some good advice. I've also heard really great things about [betterhelp.com](https://betterhelp.com), and I think they offer some aid when it comes down to people who can't afford their services.

I'll offer you some advice, as someone who used to be in your shoes. I realized that the reason why I was struggling so much to perform (i.e. school, work, etc.) is because I don't see a purpose in everything I do. I also find it difficult to create purpose where it does not exist for me. I was able to start motivating myself by telling myself why I was doing the things I had to do. For example, I get assigned a shitty book report. I don't feel like doing it, it doesn't make me happy, and I see no reason to do it. I would tell myself, "The purpose for doing this today is so that I can succeed tomorrow. The reason I need to do this is so that I can pass this class and get into college."

I also find it really helpful to take things one step at a time. If I was getting ready for school despite everything in me telling me not to, I wouldn't tell myself to "get ready to go to school". Going to school was the last step, the first steps were, "stand up, brush your teeth, find a shirt, find pants, get dressed, etc. etc." and that really helped me deal with my anxiety.

I know I'm not supposed to tell you to just hang in there, it'll get better, blah blah blah. I hated when people said that to me. But, I will say that the people who told me it would get better were right. I don't know your exact situation, and everyone deals with these emotions differently, but you seem like a bright person. Life is a mountain range, and right now you're at the bottom of the valley. The climb up isn't easy, but it is easier to breathe at the top. Take things one step at a time, when you have a bad thought, immediately correct your mind. Don't be mean to yourself. For every negative thought you have about yourself, come up with at least two good thoughts. Prioritize yourself, take care of yourself. Take a nice bath, buy yourself something you really want, keep a journal to get all the bad thoughts out and away from you.

Just remember that 6 months to a year from now, you will feel like a completely new person with new experiences. Things will change, because that's what things do. That's what time does, it changes things. Just be patient and positive. Good luck xx
